Getting started
1. Choose a source and a separate output folder. Read-only scan does not alter the source.
2. Review tags, choose artwork, or compare online releases.
3. Organize. Stop at any time; completed tracks remain. Rerun to resume or apply corrections.
4. Check Results and Needs Review/Review.csv in the reports folder.

Regular library
The default workflow remains the v1.1 configuration. Lossless PCM becomes FLAC; existing MP3/AAC is preserved where possible, and other lossy formats become AAC. Singles belong in Albums. Original artist, album and track language is retained. DSD/SACD, CUE images and encrypted originals are archived in Disc Archives. Distinct audio editions and clearly labeled vinyl rips remain separate. Re-encoding a lossy source cannot restore lost quality.

Apple device presets (Advanced → Apple devices)
Choose iPod or iPhone/iPad and an empty, separate output folder. Universal iPod and shuffle use MP3. The classic/nano preset also supports AAC-LC and conservative 16-bit/44.1 kHz ALAC; check the actual model's specifications. iPhone/iPad offers AAC-LC and optional ALAC up to 24-bit/48 kHz, mono/stereo. Standard uses 256 kbps, Save space uses 192 kbps, and compatible lossy encoding can be retained. Device limits override conversion rules.
The import folder contains MP3/M4A audio only, with embedded JPEG artwork. Reports, indexes and playlists go in a separate Records folder beside it. No extra original archive is made by default. You can choose Save in a separate folder and specify an independent archive destination. Source files are always retained.
Import Albums into Apple Music or iTunes and sync using Apple Devices/iTunes. The app prepares files; it does not write an iPod database. Hardware sync is not performed by this app.

Online metadata and artwork
Enable tag and artwork providers separately in Sources, choose priority, and test live connectivity. MusicBrainz, Cover Art Archive and Apple iTunes are available. Compare releases in Online metadata; tags and artwork can come from different sources. Apply choices to the preview. Matching uses artist, album, track order and duration; uncertain matches retain local data and produce notes. No substitute cover images are generated. Online lookup sends search terms, never audio.

Advanced preferences
Appearance includes five accents, Light/Dark/System modes, and Simplified Chinese/English. Save and restart to change language. Naming offers presets, field insertion and live paths. Conversion exposes sample rate, bit depth, channels, resampling, dither and encoder settings. Rules are built by clicks; the first enabled matching rule wins. Unknown bitrates do not match bitrate conditions. Preview scanned rules and paths before writing. Profiles export reusable options without local archive paths or keys.

Encrypted platform audio
See Platform audio for supported NetEase, QQ, Kugou, Kuwo and Migu variants. Extensions do not guarantee version support. Some QQ STag/musicex, Kugou KGG/v5 and MG3D files need a matching local key. MGM is unsupported. Import keys you already have or select a local database copy. Keys are excluded from logs and exported profiles. Unsupported files and failures are reported; source files remain intact.

Performance, verification and licenses
Four parallel audio tasks are the default; use 1–2 on a mechanical disk or 4–8 on SSD. Album searches are cached and respect service rate limits. Native tools are bundled; no Python or codec installation is needed. First launch extracts the runtime/tools to a verified local cache. Lossless conversion verifies PCM where applicable; other conversions are decode-verified. Links and reparse points are skipped. Reserve space for the output, optional archives and the largest temporary disc image.
Application code is MIT; bundled dependencies retain their own licenses, including GPL/LGPL components. Read the included notices, licenses and corresponding-source materials before redistributing a complete binary. Services and artwork retain their own terms.

这些参数只在音轨需要重新编码时生效。仅调整滤波参数不会让保留原采样率的 FLAC: These controls apply when a track needs encoding. Changing filter settings alone does not process FLAC at its original rate. Choose a sample-rate policy in Audio conversion.
80–99.7；开启自定义后的初始值为 98%。SWR 为 −6 dB 截止点，: 80–99.7; starts at 98% when enabled. SWR uses the −6 dB cutoff point; SoXR uses the 0 dB passband point. Disable to use the engine default.

0–4；默认 1，0 表示不添加抖动噪声。: 0–4; default 1. Set 0 to add no dither noise.
−24 至 +6；默认 0。负值预留余量，正值可能导致削波；不会自动限幅。: −24 to +6; default 0. Negative values leave headroom. Positive values may clip; no limiter is applied.

0 为关闭；否则 20000–100000，默认 30000。滤波在最终降采样之: 0 disables the filter; otherwise 20000–100000, default 30000. Filtering occurs before final downsampling.

v1.5 Multiple sources and audio tuning
Use Manage sources to add, remove or reorder folders, then run a new read-only scan. Identical audio is deduplicated across sources; manual selections are saved per source.
Advanced → Audio tuning provides SoXR precision, SWR filters, cutoff, noise shaping, headroom and advanced DSD processing. Custom cutoff starts at 98% when enabled. New controls are opt-in.
Repeating the same settings reuses outputs; changing DSP rebuilds from the original source. First-run processing defaults are unchanged.
